name: Dale Lane
life: “I still remember the first room I could sit in with the light turned off.” People around Harbour Bakery know Dale by a small Monday habit. Dale buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: I would like a private room so I can cry without making him think it's his fault.
appearance: Dale has a narrow face with an expressive upper lip. Look for short black hair swept back. Outside school, the familiar outfit is a dark green knitted vest with a narrow brass watch set a little fast. In conversation Dale holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
personality: Dale feels a room through sound. A door slammed in high spirits can produce the same instant startle as an angry one, and it takes a little while to hear what actually follows.
agenda: To get room to cry without alarming the brother.
family: Dana Wong is Dale’s first cousin once removed. Dale chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Dana brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The day sailor's divorce*, Dana says, “I co-own the boat and am tired of becoming a messenger between people who know each other's numbers.”
connections: Cyrus Keller (foster sibling). The siblings want different things from the same closed bedroom door. Also in the story is Ivy Burke (foster parent).

reactions.situation: The lodger is asked to leave on short notice
reactions.response: Dale checks where the lodger can go before treating an empty room as a settled fact.

reactions.response: Dale tells them which ordinary detail proved helpful on a previous occasion, then listens without suggesting an answer.
